title: Mapped-single comparison and inverse single shift
statement: Let B,C be abelian categories, C with a chosen derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], G : B → C additive, X an object of B and n a natural number. Put K_i = single_i(X) in K⁺(B), h : K_n → K_0[-n] the inverse single shift, M = G.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus, and m_i : Qh(M(K_i)) ≅ single_i(G(X)) the canonical mapped-single comparison. Then m_n hom followed by the inverse single shift in D⁺(C) equals Qh(M(h)), followed by Qh of M.commShiftIso(-n) hom at K_0, Qh.commShiftIso(-n) hom at M(K_0), and the shift by -n of m_0 hom. No enough-injectives, exactness, or derived category assumption on B is required.

proof.text: Apply the faithful derived inclusion and unfold the mapped-single comparisons as Q applied to the coefficient isomorphisms. Expand the lifted single shift. Postcompose by the inclusion shift hom; naturality moves the shifted mapped-single comparison past it.

Compute both the bounded-below Qh shift and the bounded-below mapped-functor shift under their inclusions using Functor.CommShift.OfComp.map_iso_hom_app. Expand the homotopy inverse single shift with the inverse-lift formula, and cancel the inclusion shift comparisons. Use naturality of the ambient Qh shift comparison for the degree-zero mapped-single morphism; the remaining equation is Qh applied to an equation in the homotopy category.

Expand homotopy single shifts as postcomposition of cochain single shifts by the quotient. NatTrans.shift_app_comm for G.mapHomotopyCategoryFactors supplies compatibility of the two quotient shift comparisons. Quotient shift naturality for the degree-zero coefficient isomorphism reduces to the image of an equality of cochain morphisms. Apply the upstream proved Functor.mapHomologicalComplex_map_singleFunctors_shiftIso_hom_app (WeilConjectures/Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/HomotopyCategory/SingleFunctors.lean, lines 29–44): precompose by the image of the forward single shift, cancel its inverse, and cancel the target forward/inverse shifts. This gives the required inverse equation in a few lines, including n=0 and X=0.

lean.statement:
theorem mapped_single_inverse_shift (G : B ⥤ C) [G.Additive] (X : B) (n : ℕ) :
    let K₀ := (HomotopyCategory.Plus.singleFunctor B 0).obj X
    let h := ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.singleFunctors B).shiftIso
      (-(n : ℤ)) n 0 (by simp)).inv.app X
    (G.mapHomotopyCategoryPlusSingleFunctorQhObjIso n X).hom ≫
      ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctors C).shiftIso
        (-(n : ℤ)) n 0 (by simp)).inv.app (G.obj X) =
    DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh.map (G.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus.map h) ≫
      DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh.map
        ((G.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus.commShiftIso (-(n : ℤ))).hom.app K₀) ≫
      (DerivedCategory.Plus.Qh.commShiftIso (-(n : ℤ))).hom.app
        (G.mapHomotopyCategoryPlus.obj K₀) ≫
      ((G.mapHomotopyCategoryPlusSingleFunctorQhObjIso 0 X).hom)⟦-(n : ℤ)⟧'
